holidays.name: Eight Track Tape Day
holidays.description: A nostalgic nod to the chunky, clunky cartridge that once blasted road-trip anthems from dashboards everywhere. Dig out your vintage tapes and enjoy the mid-song track changes, which come with a loud, satisfying kerchunk.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrated by retro music fans and collectors.
holidays.funFact: Eight-track tapes often split songs in the middle. The tape's looping design forced a track change wherever the program ran out, even mid-guitar solo.

holidays.name: National Cheese Fondue Day
holidays.description: A day for gathering around a bubbling pot of melted cheese and dunking bread, veggies, and cured meats into it. It's hard to beat as a social, gooey, and slightly competitive way to eat dinner.
holidays.origin: Cheese fondue comes from Switzerland, where it dates to the early 19th century. Historians think it began as a thrifty peasant meal made from cheese and leftover bread.
holidays.funFact: The traditional fondue pot is called a caquelon. It is a heavy earthenware vessel that spreads heat evenly and keeps the cheese smooth.

holidays.name: International "Louie Louie" Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the garage-rock classic that has been shouted, slurred, and mangled by bar bands for decades. Crank it up and sing along, even if you're making up the words.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, created by fans of the much-covered rock and roll song.
holidays.funFact: The FBI investigated the song in the 1960s over rumors that its muddy lyrics were obscene. The investigation reportedly found the words impossible to make out.
